title: Non-human identities: who owns each service account and key, and when is it rotated?
short: Give every service account, app secret and API key an owner and a rotation date, and cap Entra app secrets at 180 days.
answer: Within 90 days, list every service account, app registration, API key and token with an owner and a rotation date, and block or cap new secrets in policy. Then replace each static secret with a managed identity or federation wherever the platform supports it, and rotate the rest on a schedule your policies enforce.
audience: IT, cloud and security teams on Microsoft 365, Azure, AWS or Google Cloud, with or without on-premises Active Directory

blocks.title: If you only do five things

items.title: List every non-human identity with an owner and a rotation date.
items.text: Add purpose, permissions and a review date[^svcgov]. Improper offboarding tops OWASP's list of NHI risks[^owaspnhi].

items.title: Replace static secrets with federation.
items.text: Use managed identities in Azure, which are free[^mi], and federation elsewhere, as Microsoft, AWS and Google advise[^wif][^awsbp][^gcpkeys].

items.title: Block or cap secrets in policy.
items.text: Block new Entra client secrets or cap them at 180 days[^scuba], exempting apps that still need them[^amp]. Rotate Google keys: expiry can cause outages[^gcpkeys].

items.title: Log what they do.
items.text: Send service principal and managed identity sign-ins to your SIEM[^scuba]. Intruders who compromise a person's account go looking for service principals and API keys[^mddr].

items.title: Move on-premises services to gMSAs.
items.text: Their passwords change every 30 days[^gmsasec]. Ordinary service accounts invite Kerberoasting[^dmsa].

items.title: Export Entra apps and their credentials.
items.text: List app registrations, service principals and managed identities with credential type and end date. Treat those with privileged roles as Tier 0, as the privileged-access sheet describes.

items.title: Pull the cloud credential reports.
items.text: The AWS report lists access keys and their last use but skips service-specific credentials such as Bedrock long-term API keys[^awscred]. In Google Cloud, list user-managed service account keys. The cloud configuration sheet covers removing cloud keys.

items.title: Search AD for service accounts.
items.text: Look for user accounts with SPNs, delegation or passwords that never expire[^svcuser].

items.title: Ask about the rest.
items.text: SaaS API keys, GitHub tokens and deploy keys, SSH keys, what your IT provider set up, CI secrets (see the supply-chain sheet) and agents (see the agentic AI sheet). Check sign-ins, disable what nobody claims, delete it after a set period[^svcgov].

blocks.title: Replace static secrets, platform by platform
items: **Azure: managed identities.** Where an app registration is unavoidable, use a managed identity as its federated credential[^mi].
**Into Entra: federated credentials.** They accept tokens from GitHub Actions, Kubernetes, Google Cloud, AWS and SPIFFE[^wif].
**Into AWS: roles.** From outside AWS, use IAM Roles Anywhere with an X.509 certificate, or `AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity`[^awsbp].
**Into Google Cloud: Workload Identity Federation.** Then block key creation; organizations created before 3 May 2024 may not block it by default[^gcpbase].

**Secrets that must stay: your platform's store.** Key Vault, AWS Secrets Manager or Google Secret Manager, each with a rotation schedule. Key Vault can trigger rotation 30 days before expiry[^akvrot]. Encryption keys are in the encryption sheet.

**Self-hosted stores: check the license.** HashiCorp Vault's Business Source License allows internal production use, but not a competing hosted or embedded paid offering[^vaultlic]. OpenBao, a fork managed by the Linux Foundation's OpenSSF[^openbao], uses the open-source MPL 2.0[^baolic].

blocks.title: Service accounts in Active Directory
items: **Prefer gMSAs and dMSAs.** A Windows Server 2025 dMSA replaces a service account and disables its password, so every machine using it must support dMSA[^dmsa]. Keep user accounts out of privileged groups[^svcuser].

**Patch BadSuccessor.** With a Windows Server 2025 DC, the right to create a dMSA in an OU let users take over any account. Users outside Domain Admins held it in 91% of environments Akamai examined[^akamai]. Install the August 2025 fix (CVE-2025-53779)[^msrc], limit dMSA creation to trusted admins and audit events 5137 and 5136[^akamai].
**Guard the KDS root key as Tier 0.** Whoever reads it can compute gMSA and dMSA passwords offline, unlogged by default. Audit reads of `msKds-RootKeyData`[^semperis].

items.title: Revoke it where it was issued.
items.text: Add a new credential, switch over, then delete the leaked one, or all of them if unsure[^wlrisk]. Deleting it from the repository isn't enough[^gcpkeys]; for scanning, see the attack-surface sheet.

items.title: Check whether it was used.
items.text: Search sign-in and audit logs since the leak for unusual sign-ins, new credentials, configuration changes and app roles[^wlrisk].

items.title: Rotate what it could reach.
items.text: Include vault secrets the identity could read[^wlrisk] and, if a developer machine leaked it, that machine's SSH, API and cloud keys[^mddr].

blocks.title: Monitoring, and the licenses it needs
items: **Keep the logs.** Entra keeps sign-ins 7 days on Free and 30 on P1 or P2. Graph activity logs need P1 or P2 and an export[^entralogs].
**Read the detections.** ID Protection flags leaked app credentials and anomalous activity, but not for managed identities[^wlrisk].

**Pay for details and blocking.** Workload ID Premium, $3 per workload identity a month[^wlfaq], adds full risk details[^wlrisk] and Conditional Access by location or risk for your own single-tenant apps[^wlca].

blocks.title: What changed in 2026
items: **Agents got their own identities.** Entra Agent ID became generally available in April 2026, and Lifecycle Workflows can hand sponsorship to a leaver's manager[^entranew]. Entra security features for agents need Agent 365[^agentid].
**CISA set credential limits.** ScubaGear 2.0 recommends app secrets of up to 180 days and certificates up to 365 (enter 181 and 366)[^scuba].
**AWS federates outward.** Since November 2025, workloads can use short-lived tokens instead of stored API keys for external services[^awsout].

blocks.title: What you can skip
items: **An NHI security platform before a list.** Credential reports and sign-in logs hold most of the data. Buy tooling once owners are named.
**Workload ID Premium everywhere.** Its Conditional Access covers only your own single-tenant apps[^wlca]. Buy it for privileged ones.
**Vaulting secrets you could delete.** A vaulted secret is still a secret, and a self-hosted vault is one more Tier 0 system.

blocks.title: Mistakes that cost the most
items: **One person as the only owner.** Name a team too, or a leaver orphans it.
**Expecting a policy to fix old credentials.** Entra app management policies leave existing apps and their secrets working[^amp].
**Trusting private repositories.** GitGuardian's vendor report found secrets in 32.2% of internal repositories and 5.6% of public ones[^gg].

blocks.title: What this looks like at your size

columns.title: Small team, no security staff
items: Keep the inventory in a shared spreadsheet; review it quarterly.
Block new Entra client secrets (free, per Microsoft's FAQ[^wlfaq]), exempting apps that need them[^amp].

columns.title: Growing, with IT or security staff
items: Alert on new app credentials and on interactive service account sign-ins.
Move AD services to gMSAs, starting with accounts that have SPNs.

columns.title: Enterprise or regulated
items: Buy Workload ID Premium for privileged apps; reviewing them needs P2 for reviewers[^wlfaq].
Give each AI agent a sponsor who confirms twice a year that it's still needed.
